sponsor: Office of the Secretary of War, executed by DIU, NSWC Crane and the Test Resource Management Center
stage: 19 companies advancing to Gauntlet II, Fort Carson CO, August 2026
funnel: 26 companies in Gauntlet I, 49 in the Phase 2 Qualifier (Camp Grayling MI, June 8-19 2026), 19 to Gauntlet II
requirement: Each company must deliver 120 kamikaze drones with lethality payloads in roughly five weeks. Price ceilings $5,500 long-range strike, $4,500 close quarters. Awards cover 5 long-range and 3 close-quarters designs, with production orders of 4,000-9,500 UAVs per winner.
why_it_matters: Nineteen pre-qualified companies that must prove they can manufacture at wartime speed. Every one is a Stratasys prospect. The 120-units-in-five-weeks requirement is the additive manufacturing pitch stated as a procurement requirement. Intelligence indicates HP is supporting 14 of the 19 [validation-needed]; if true, HP is buying ecosystem position ahead of its advertising, which no ad scan would surface.
headline_signal: Formlabs is confirmed inside ORQA, a Gauntlet II company, and claims SkyFall, which builds the drone that won Gauntlet I for Skycutter.

sources.t: DOD names 19 companies invited to Phase II final demo
Formlabs case study: drone solutions with SLS at ORQA FPV
Skycutter tops Gauntlet I leaderboard with SkyFall-built Shrike 10F
Inside Neros' factory: why printing does not solve the supply chain

teams.notes: CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson, on a factory tour: '3D printing is generally good for making a few of a thing, making lots of different things. We are mostly focused on making a lot of one thing, or a really consistent process.' And: 'You're not gonna be 3D printing your circuit boards, your motors, your radios, any of that stuff out on the battlefield. So it does not solve the supply chain problem.' Read it precisely. He is rejecting distributed printing as a supply-chain fix, not rejecting additive inside a factory. That is a narrower claim than it sounds and it is answerable.
teams.backing: VC-backed. Founded 2023 by former professional drone racers Soren Monroe-Anderson and Olaf Hichwa.
teams.scale: Moved from a 15,000 sq ft site to a 250,000 sq ft factory (Millennium One). 250+ drones/day today, targeting 1M/year. Highest-output American drone manufacturer in 2025.
teams.tech: Vertically integrated conventional mass manufacturing. Explicitly designs the product around the process rather than around printing.
teams.sales_hook: Do not lead with speed-to-part. Lead with tooling-free bridge production and design changes mid-programme. Their public objection is about printing at the edge, not about additive in the factory. That distinction is the opening.

teams.notes: Robinson ownership changes the sale. Sell to the parent's manufacturing engineering function.
teams.backing: Acquired by Robinson Helicopter Company, April 2024. Prior funding was a 2019 seed led by Dreamit and a 2015 Kickstarter for the Sprite.
teams.scale: Builds through Robinson's vertically integrated manufacturing operation in California.
teams.tech: Rugged cylindrical coaxial VTOL drones for industrial, public safety and defense.
teams.sales_hook: Owned by a real aerospace manufacturer, which means an existing quality system and an existing supply chain. The buying centre is Robinson, not Ascent. Coaxial cylindrical airframes are geometrically awkward for conventional tooling, which is a genuine additive argument rather than a generic one.

teams.notes: The $25M of DoW non-dilutive capital is the signal. The Pentagon is directly funding the autonomy layer it wants standardised across vendors.
teams.backing: $130M Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners, Sept 2025, including $25M non-dilutive from the Department of War via the Office of Strategic Capital. Lakestar, Mosaic Ventures and Costanoa Ventures also participated.
teams.scale: Software-first. Strategy is 'build swarms, not individual drones' through AuterionOS and the Nemyx defense system.
teams.tech: Skynode and Skynode X autonomy modules, AI autonomy, secure comms, edge computing, jamming resilience. Priced like consumer electronics.
teams.sales_hook: Software company, not an airframe manufacturer, so the printer sale is not to them directly. The value is the map: Auterion knows which airframe builders it is designed into. Treat this as a channel and intelligence relationship, not a hardware deal.

teams.notes: Founder-owned since 1995. Shortest decision chain on the board.
teams.hq: Madison, Alabama, USA, in the Huntsville defense cluster.
teams.backing: Privately held. Founded 1995 by Larry A. French, who remains Owner, CEO and CTO.
teams.scale: Long-standing target-drone and UAS manufacturer with an established DoD vendor history.
teams.tech: MQM-170 Outlaw, Valiant and related UAS platforms.
teams.sales_hook: The incumbent on this list. Thirty years of DoD delivery and a founder-owner who still holds CTO, so one person can approve a capital purchase. Huntsville proximity makes it an easy field visit. Legacy aerospace processes mean tooling and lead-time pain is real and quantifiable.

teams.notes: Autonomy and compute supplier rather than a mass airframe producer. 'Hand built in San Diego' is stated openly, which is a direct opening for tooling-free production.
teams.hq: Sorrento Valley, San Diego, California, USA
teams.backing: Spun out of Qualcomm in 2018. Over $18.7M in government contracts. About 44 employees, reporting at least 60% annual sales growth.
teams.scale: All drones hand built in San Diego. Small headcount, high growth.
teams.tech: VOXL 2 autopilot on Qualcomm QRB5165 at 16g, VOXL 2 Mini at 11g and 42x42mm, VOXL 3 thermal AI processing. Runs PX4. GPS-denied autonomy.
teams.sales_hook: Hand built at 44 people is the definition of a company that cannot tool. Size, weight and power constrained enclosures for 11g compute modules are a precision additive application. Small deal size, fast decision, good reference logo.

teams.notes: Formlabs runs a conversation ad claiming 'Skyfall, the largest drone manufacturer in Ukraine, uses our printers to deploy flight-ready parts the same day they're designed.' Independently, Skycutter's Gauntlet I entry, the Shrike 10F, is made by SkyFall. Neither source confirms the other, so the link is [Unverified], but it is the highest-value thing to verify on this board.
teams.backing: Private UK company. On contract for more than 2,500 drones off Gauntlet I.
teams.scale: Won Gauntlet I outright with 99.3 of 100 points, about 12 points clear of Neros in second.
teams.tech: Fielded the Shrike 10F, a 10-inch fibre-optic FPV drone developed and manufactured by SkyFall of Ukraine. Skycutter provided logistics and engineering support.
teams.sales_hook: Highest-priority account on this list. It topped Gauntlet I and its airframe comes from SkyFall, the manufacturer Formlabs names in outbound as a printer customer. If that claim is true, a competitor is already inside the number one team's supply chain. Verify before assuming, then call SkyFall as well as Skycutter.

teams.notes: A greenfield US facility with a public jobs commitment is the clearest capital-equipment buying window among the 19.
teams.hq: US entity for Ukraine's F-Drones. First US plant in Holland, Lucas County, Ohio.
teams.backing: $18.4M committed investment in the Ohio facility with at least 300 jobs pledged by Dec 31 2029. Announced with Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur.
teams.scale: F10 quadcopter scored 72.9 of 100 in Gauntlet I, which secured a US Army procurement contract. Among the 11 selected for follow-on orders.
teams.sales_hook: Best-timed account on the list. They are building a brand new US plant right now with public money attached and jobs promised. Equipment decisions for that line are being made this year. Get in before the line is specified.

teams.notes: Public parent means quarterly disclosure. Red Cat earnings calls are a free intelligence feed on the whole segment.
teams.backing: Wholly owned subsidiary of Red Cat Holdings, Nasdaq: RCAT. Sister company FlightWave Aerospace.
teams.scale: $2.49M US Air Force firm-fixed-price order for Black Widow systems, July 2026. Black Widow selected on competitive tender by an Asia-Pacific ally (Dec 2025) and a NATO ally (March 2026), both delivering in 2026.
teams.tech: Black Widow sUAS. American-made hardware and software.
teams.sales_hook: The only publicly listed pure-play on the board, so the financials are readable and the pressure is quarterly. Multiple allied deliveries landing in the same year is a capacity problem. Lead with surge capacity and second-source resilience.

teams.notes: Missed a Gauntlet I delivery order and came back for Gauntlet II. A company with something to prove and a 3.5x capacity ramp in front of it.
teams.backing: Spun out of Firefly Drone Shows in August 2024. CEO Kyle Dorosz.
teams.scale: Current capacity 72,000 units a year, scaling to 250,000+. Fully NDAA-compliant supply chain. Competed in Gauntlet I but did not win a delivery order, then qualified for Gauntlet II.
teams.tech: Proprietary swarm coordination software allowing one operator to fly thousands of drones without collisions. Heritage in entertainment drone shows.
teams.sales_hook: Scaling from 72K to 250K units a year is a tooling decision they have to make soon, and they missed a Gauntlet I order so the pressure is on. Detroit location means automotive manufacturing talent and automotive assumptions about tooling. Bring the cost-per-part crossover analysis.

teams.notes: Research gap. Identity ambiguity is the blocker, not absence of information. Resolve the entity first.
teams.hq: Not established from public sources. Appears in reporting as Vector Defense. [Unverified]
teams.scale: Advanced from the Gauntlet I field of 25 to the Gauntlet II field of 19.
teams.sales_hook: Name collision with several unrelated companies called Vector makes open-source research unreliable. Confirm the legal entity from the DIU or NSWC Crane vendor listing before any outreach.

teams.notes: Going public at $1.5B. Post-listing they will need auditable, documented manufacturing processes, which favours a qualified system over an open-material one.
teams.hq: Israel, with US headquarters and a drone production facility in Tampa, Florida.
teams.backing: $70M Series B completed with a $30M extension co-led by Aliya Capital Partners and Protego Ventures, July 2025. Earlier $40M including Chartered Group and General-Tech. Founded 2018 by Matteo Shapira, Rubi Liani and Adir Tubi.
teams.scale: Announced a Nasdaq listing at a $1.5B valuation via all-stock merger with JFB Construction Holdings, closing mid-2026, to be renamed XTEND AI Robotics, ticker XTND.
teams.tech: Human-guided autonomous machine systems, battle-proven AI robots for defense.
teams.sales_hook: Newly built US production facility in Tampa plus a public listing means capex and scrutiny at the same time. New facilities buy new capability. Go now, while the Tampa line is still being tooled.

teams.notes: Eric Schmidt-backed. The $500M IDIQ is the largest single funding event among the 19 and makes this the highest-budget prospect on the list.
teams.backing: Backed by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Launched quietly in 2023 as White Stork. $500M IDIQ from the Department of War, May 2026, one of the largest counter-UAS awards ever made to a non-incumbent. Earlier $5.2M with JIATF-401, Jan 2026.
teams.scale: Scaling against a $500M ceiling. Interceptors proven in Ukraine.
teams.tech: Merops interceptors, Bumblebee quadcopters, Hornet midrange strike drones. AI-powered counter-UAS.
teams.sales_hook: Best-funded name on the board and the money is fresh. A $500M IDIQ means a production ramp they have not built yet, which is exactly when tooling-free capacity gets bought. Go early and go at the program office, not the lab.

teams.notes: Blue UAS Cleared listing removes the biggest US procurement barrier. European base, so route through the EMEA team.
teams.backing: Founded and staffed by former operators of the Jaeger Corps and Fromandskorpset, Danish special forces.
teams.scale: Delivered at least 10,000 Nightmare FPV systems to Ukraine's Ministry of Defence, mostly since October 2025.
teams.tech: Nightmare FPV, on the Blue UAS Cleared List in analog and digital variants. Also builds portable counter-drone systems.
teams.sales_hook: Their stated method is design, build, test, improve, with prototypes going straight to the front and coming back modified within days. That is an iteration-rate argument, which is the single strongest additive argument there is. Sell the loop, not the part.

teams.notes: 70,000 drones a month across 33 products is a part-number problem as much as a volume problem, and part-number proliferation is where tooling economics break down.
teams.hq: Joint venture. Production at Wilcox Industries' complex in Newington, New Hampshire, USA. General Cherry is Ukrainian.
teams.backing: Joint venture announced March 2026 between General Cherry and Wilcox Industries. Still in the approval phase, seeking Ukrainian state backing before formal registration. [Unverified] as to completion.
teams.scale: General Cherry, founded September 2023, produces more than 70,000 drones a month across 33 codified products.
teams.tech: FPV and interceptor drones. Bullet interceptor, a 309 km/h fixed-wing VTOL built to engage Shahed-class attack drones, plus the AIR counter-UAV series. General Cherry engineering leads development, Wilcox provides manufacturing infrastructure and US procurement access.
teams.sales_hook: A new US production line being stood up from scratch in New Hampshire, explicitly aimed at Pentagon orders. Same timing logic as the Ohio plant. The engineering team is Ukrainian and used to fast iteration, the facility is American and needs documented process. That gap is the sale.

teams.notes: Production volume figures differ by roughly an order of magnitude between sources. Do not quote a number externally.
teams.scale: Reported deliveries of up to 15,000 units a month to the Ukrainian market, with wider reporting of far higher figures. Tens of thousands of UAVs fielded. Volume claims vary widely by source. [Unverified]
teams.tech: Combat FPV strike drones built to operate under electronic warfare and carry heavier payloads at range. Models include Grim, Volyniaka and Hromylo, plus 8 inch and 10 inch FPV platforms.
teams.sales_hook: High-volume Ukrainian producer under wartime tempo. Additive competes with injection tooling on time-to-first-part, not unit cost. Expect an export-control and end-use review before any conversation goes far.

teams.notes: Research gap. Generic company name makes open-source search unusable. Carry to next run.
teams.scale: Advanced to Gauntlet II at Fort Carson, August 2026.
teams.sales_hook: Confirmed in the programme, invisible in public sources. Same treatment as Vector: get the entity from the programme vendor listing first.

teams.notes: Three organisations, two mission areas. Map the buying centre carefully before pitching.
teams.hq: Mountain Horse Solutions, USA. AG3 Labs spun out of Michigan State University. Draganfly is a partner.
teams.backing: AG3 Labs won $350K as one of four global winners at Army xTechCounter Strike in Germany. Founded by MSU students.
teams.scale: Three-way team. Competing in both mission areas.
teams.tech: Draganfly Flex FPV drone for Mission Area A, long-range strike at 5 to 20 km beyond visual line of sight. AG3 SPADE plus Flex for Mission Area B, tactical work in buildings, trenches and tunnels under 2 km. AG3 builds low-cost swarming quadcopters with repeatable flight patterns for training.
teams.sales_hook: The only team on the board competing in both mission areas, which means two airframe families and twice the part count. AG3's low-cost swarm training drones are a volume consumable play. Draganfly is the manufacturing partner and probably the real buying centre.

teams.notes: Formlabs published case study, July 9 2025. ORQA prints electronic speed controllers, antennae, flight controls, goggle prototypes, camera mounts, drone frames and propeller guards, including end-use parts. Buys powder in 50 kg lots and keeps 100 kg on hand to avoid interrupting production batches. Mechanical designer Antonio Kovac: 'With the Fuse 1+ we can get prints the same day. We don't need to wait for changes in tooling.' This is the clearest confirmed competitor placement inside a Gauntlet account.
teams.hq: Osijek, Croatia. US entity ORQA US LLC.
teams.backing: EUR 12.7M Series A led by Expeditions Ventures, with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Taiwania Capital, Aymo and Radius Capital. Earlier EUR 5.8M seed. Founded 2018 by Srdjan Kovacevic, Ivan Jelusic and Vlatko Matijevic.
teams.scale: Croatian facility rated up to 280,000 NDAA-compliant drones a year, targeting 500,000 drones and components. EUR 10M FPV contract with the Croatian military. Supplied Ukrainian forces.
teams.tech: Builds flight controllers, radios, motors, cameras and PCBs in-house and avoids Chinese components for supply-chain sovereignty. Runs Formlabs Fuse 1 and Fuse 1+ 30W SLS printers on Nylon 12 and TPU 90A.
teams.sales_hook: A competitor is already installed here and Formlabs has published the case study. Do not pitch entry-level SLS. Pitch what Fuse cannot do: qualified engineering polymers, FDM for large jigs and fixtures, and repeatability across a 280K-unit-a-year line. Their own supply-chain-sovereignty argument is the wedge, because Open Material Mode pushes qualification onto them.

teams.notes: Confirmed in Gauntlet II with the Deadliner Q1. Everything else is unestablished. Research gap, carry to next run.
teams.tech: Deadliner Q1 UAV, its Gauntlet II entry.
teams.sales_hook: Thin public footprint. Treat as a discovery call, not a pitch. Establish who manufactures the Deadliner Q1 and where before spending time.

research_note: Enrichment pass Aug 25 2026 added headquarters, financial backing, production scale, technology and a sales hook for all 19 teams. Public sources only. Three companies (Vector, Hyperscale, Stellarion) have thin or ambiguous public footprints and are flagged as research gaps rather than filled with guesses.
